title: These are the Humanitarian Decision Makers
html:
In my June post Who are the Humanitarian Decision Makers, I outlined why I have problems with how easily we use the phrase “for the decision makers” without really knowing who they are. Once you start investigating the problem, you quickly realize how large and diverse the range of decision makers are in humanitarian response.

Now, it is easy to complain but harder to do something. So rather than leaving this problem to fester within the community, a few of us decided to do something. A first outcome of that work is version one of the Humanitarian Decision Makers Taxonomy (offline PDF full size | offline PDF A3 size  | online interactive).

We hope that from now on, this product will help people to have more structured conversations, to be able to better articulate which decision makers they are targeting, to inquire with said people to design better products, and to continue expanding (openly) on this work.

A huge amount of credit goes out to Quentin Nicaise who did the bulk of the work putting this piece together and developing the interactive version. Full credit to Ana Macau who designed the offline version. And to Jarrod Goentzel, Bartel Van de Walle, Erica Gralla and Lars Peter Nissen for their keen interest and participation in the DMN Community as well as planting the seed for the taxonomy.

The taxonomy and related work was completed by UN-OCHA as a contribution to the Decision Makers Need (DMN) Community who released it under a Creative Commons attribution license. Hopefully this means that we will see it be used for a range of purposes.

The data to complete the taxonomy has also been released so that you can recompile or restructure how you want. We envision that several more things could be done with this data to help the community - categorize decision maker types (strategic, tactical, operational, etc), group similar role types, group by geographical coverage, etc. If you have an idea, feel free to give it a try and share it back.

If you are interested in getting involved with the DMN Community, kindly see their page on the Digital Humanitarian Network website.

Andrej
